record.original_question: Let T012(a,b) denote the number of tilings of the (a,b)-benzel in which left stones are allowed, right stones are forbidden, and exactly two of the three bone orientations are allowed. Is it true that T012(3n, 3n) = 2^n n! for every n >= 1?

evidence.quote: For 0 <= i, j <= 1 and 0 <= k <= 3 we define Tijk (a, b) as the number of ways to tile the (a, b)-benzel if the set of allowed prototiles contains the right stone iff i = 1, contains the left stone iff j = 1, and contains k of the bones. We say that such a tiling is an i, j, k tiling.
Problem 2: Is it true that T012 (3n, 3n) = 2^n n! for n >= 1?
Comment: Colin Defant, Rupert Li, Benjamin Young and I worked on problem 2 during the conference and later succeeded in solving Problems 2 and 3; see [3].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the (a,b)-benzel, a hexagonal-style region in the triangular lattice depending on positive integers a,b. The allowed prototiles are: a "left stone" and a "right stone" (two shapes of 2-cell tiles), together with "bones," which come in three possible orientations (each a 3-cell straight tribone, one per direction of the triangular lattice). For 0 ≤ i,j ≤ 1 and 0 ≤ k ≤ 3, let T_{ijk}(a,b) denote the number of tilings of the (a,b)-benzel using prototiles from the set that includes the right stone iff i=1, the left stone iff j=1, and exactly k of the three bone orientations (one specifies which k of the three are allowed; the count T_{ijk} sums over the symmetry-equivalent classes as conventionally defined).

In the case (i,j,k) = (0,1,2): right stones are forbidden, left stones are allowed, and exactly two of the three bone orientations are allowed. Prove or disprove:
$$T_{012}(3n,3n) = 2^n\, n!\quad\text{for every integer } n \geq 1.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture was resolved by Defant, Li, Propp, and Young in subsequent work on benzel tilings (developed via the abacus bijection and generalized compression methods). The original problem statement was annotated as solved, and follow-up papers (arXiv:2209.05717 "Tilings of Benzels via the Abacus Bijection" and arXiv:2403.07663 "Tilings of Benzels via Generalized Compression") establish the relevant enumeration formulas.

status_evidence.title: Tilings of Benzels via the Abacus Bijection
status_evidence.snippet: Defant, Li, Propp, Young develop the abacus bijection to enumerate benzel tilings, resolving conjectures including T012(3n,3n) formulas.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is proven in follow-up work by Defant, Li, Propp, and Young.

status_evidence.title: Tilings of Benzels via Generalized Compression
status_evidence.snippet: Generalized compression methods resolve further benzel tiling enumeration conjectures of Propp.
status_evidence.claim: Provides confirmation/extension of the T_{ijk} enumeration program.
